title: Domain growth in lipid membranes and the budding instability
authors: Jean Wolff, Fabrice Thalmann, Carlos Marques, David Andelman, Haim Diamant, Shigeyuki Komura
abstract: We investigate the growth of a circular domain in a phase-separating lipid membrane and its relation to the budding instability. We describe the in-plane dynamics with a conserved, time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau model under radial symmetry. Numerical solutions show a crossover of the domain size $D$ as a function of time $t$ from $D\sim t^{1/3}$ at early times to $D\sim t^{1/2}$ at later times, followed by saturation due to finite system size. The time-dependent line tension $σ(t)$, evaluated from the evolving concentration profile, rises rapidly before approaching the planar-interface value. This behavior distinguishes an early line-tension-dominated regime from a later domain-size-dominated regime. To estimate the budding instability, we combine $D(t)$ and $σ(t)$ with a quasistatic criterion for the loss of stability of a partially budded domain. The budding-instability time decreases with increasing membrane spontaneous curvature and increases near the critical point. Thus, the evolution of both domain size and line tension is essential for determining the time required for the budding instability.
summary: This work models domain growth in phase-separating lipid membranes using a conserved Ginzburg-Landau approach. It tracks the crossover in domain growth dynamics ($D \sim t^{1/3}$ to $D \sim t^{1/2}$) and shows that the onset of membrane budding instability depends crucially on the coupled, time-varying evolution of both domain size and line tension.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics of domain growth in phase-separating lipid membranes and how this evolution dictates the onset time of the budding instability.
main_result: The budding instability time depends critically on the coupled, time-dependent evolution of both the domain size ($D(t)$) and the line tension ($\sigma(t)$), showing distinct growth regimes ($D \sim t^{1/3}$ to $D \sim t^{1/2}$).
method: The analysis uses numerical solutions of a conserved, time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau model under radial symmetry, combined with a quasistatic criterion for stability loss.
model_or_system: The system is a fluid lipid bilayer undergoing liquid-liquid phase separation, modeled by a conserved order parameter $\phi$ governed by a fourth-order PDE. The dynamics are studied in the context of domain growth and subsequent membrane budding.
key_observables: Domain size $D(t)$, time-dependent line tension $\sigma(t)$, and the budding function $g(t)$.
important_parameters: Spontaneous curvature ($C_0$), critical point parameters ($a/b$), and characteristic time scales ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes radial symmetry and uses a quasistatic approximation to link domain growth to the instability criterion, neglecting feedback from curvature on the pre-budding evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crossover in domain growth exponents ($t^{1/3}$ to $t^{1/2}$), the time evolution of the concentration profile $\phi(r, t)$, and the dependence of the budding time on spontaneous curvature.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the governing dynamics using a conserved Ginzburg-Landau model, then analyzes the time evolution of $D(t)$ and $\sigma(t)$ through distinct growth regimes, and finally applies these time-dependent quantities to the quasistatic criterion to predict the budding instability time.
why_interesting: The study of non-equilibrium domain growth and instability thresholds is a core topic in soft matter physics, providing quantitative models for phase separation dynamics relevant to biological membranes.
